question: If part of the gravity generated by baryons leaves our projected spacetime slice and returns along curved hidden paths, can a conservative return kernel predict apparent-dark lensing morphology and backtrack its peaks to specific baryonic origins?

field_statement.full_flux: partial_A J^A=-4*pi*G*rho_b*delta(z), where A spans x,y and one hidden route coordinate z
field_statement.meaning: full-dimensional flux remains baryon sourced; vertical departure and return can look like extra projected convergence without adding material mass
field_statement.return_kernel: R(r|L,w) proportional to exp[-(r-L)^2/(2*w^2)] and integrates to one
field_statement.backtracking: P(origin i|destination d) proportional to m_i*R(|d-x_i||L,w)
field_statement.hidden_arc_visualization: the minimal illustrative path is a semicircle with height D/2 and path length pi*D/2; this geometry is not itself observed

grid.coverage_amendment: Reduced from 110 to the largest round aperture with complete support in all four maps after a WCS-footprint-only audit; no spatial kappa morphology or score was inspected.

target_preprocessing.normalization: clip background-subtracted map at zero and unit-normalize inside score aperture
target_preprocessing.reason: suppress model-specific singular galaxy pixels and mass-sheet offsets while retaining cluster-scale morphology

selection.primary_metric: equal-map mean total-convergence Jensen-Shannon divergence on development maps
selection.lock: choose one lambda, eta, and f on Caminha plus GLAFIC; transfer unchanged to Bradac plus Williams
selection.apparent_dark_residual: subtract each map's nonnegative least-squares projection of the normalized local baryon map and clip at zero

advance_gates.interpretation_if_fail: retain the backtracking machinery but reject the isotropic single-ring return law; next add a baryon-only directional/tidal kernel, not target-specific arcs

claim_limits: Kappa maps are standard-gravity model reconstructions from overlapping lensing data, not direct dark-matter observations or statistically independent experiments.
The method holdout tests reconstruction-method transfer on one cluster, not a new cluster.
A projected route cannot reveal whether a path bends along the line of sight, in a hidden field coordinate, or through an anisotropic constitutive response.
A fitted ring scale is phenomenology, not a covariant theory; a later theory must derive it and pass raw image, galaxy, and Solar tests.
Backtracked origins are probabilistic attributions under the frozen route kernel, not observed gravity trajectories.
